note:
FEATURE / HOUSE SHOWCASE: Add a dedicated `HouseShowcase` scene for interactively exploring production house generation and socket-driven furnishing. The left panel must first let the user select a production house archetype. After a house is selected, the panel must show the production props/decorations applicable to that house and allow the user to choose a set. The right side must author and render the selected house through the real production structure/material/rendering pipeline and place the selected props only through valid production decoration/socket placement rules. The user must be able to freely move the camera around the exterior and through the interior. A Regenerate action must choose a new seed, rebuild the selected house with the same house type and prop selection, and produce a different valid generated result while preserving deterministic replay for a known seed.

BASELINE / EXISTING ARCHITECTURE: `GuildHouseProgramCatalog` currently exposes ten `GuildHouseKind` programs and maps room roles to required/optional canonical decoration archetypes; `GuildHouseFurnishedPrototypeAuthoring` already resolves room decoration placements and emits them through the production decoration/socket pipeline. Use those existing authorities rather than inventing scene-local house or prop tables. At minimum the showcase must expose every production `GuildHouseKind`; also include any other reusable production house archetypes that are already generatable with semantic room/socket data by implementation time. If production lacks one canonical enumeration boundary for those house archetypes, add the narrow reusable production registry needed for enumeration rather than making the showcase itself authoritative.

PROP APPLICABILITY: The prop list must be derived from production house programs, room/context policy, canonical decoration identity, and mount/socket compatibility. Do not present arbitrary global props as compatible merely because they can be rendered. User selection is a furnishing palette/constraint passed into production composition. If multiple selected props compete for limited sockets, the resolver must place only valid non-overlapping instances and report selected-but-unplaced items/reasons in the UI; it must never force placement with hard-coded coordinates or invalid fallback sockets. Any production-required integrated fixture that cannot be deselected must be clearly distinguished from user-selectable optional furnishing.

SEED SEMANTICS: The active seed must be visible. The same house archetype + selected prop set + seed must reproduce the same semantic house/layout/placement result. Regenerate must obtain a different seed and rerun the production generator. Where a production house generator supports structural variation, regeneration must visibly vary the house shell/room/layout details rather than only shuffling props; if seed variation is missing from a reusable generator, add it to the shared production planner rather than faking variation in this showcase.

CAMERA / UI: The left panel remains usable for house selection, prop multi-selection, current-seed display, and Regenerate. The right preview supports practical exterior and interior inspection with mouse look/orbit as appropriate plus keyboard movement/zoom/pan using existing shared camera/input systems where available. Camera controls must not require debug-only editor tooling, and entering/exiting UI focus must not strand cursor/input state.

ARCHITECTURE: Reuse production house authoring, room programs, decoration catalogs, socket compatibility/placement, materials, voxel geometry, meshing/rendering, lighting, and any shared showcase browser/camera controls that exist. `HouseShowcase` is an integration consumer only: no duplicate house catalog, duplicate prop catalog, bespoke prop geometry, scene-local socket solver, hand-authored furnishing coordinates, or parallel renderer/material stack. If the earlier PropShowcase feature has introduced reusable catalog-selection UI primitives by implementation time, reuse or factor those shared primitives rather than cloning them.

ACCEPTANCE: Complete every checkbox in `tasks.md`. Built-player evidence must demonstrate at least two materially different house archetypes, different compatible prop lists, multi-select furnishing, valid socket-driven placement including an interior view, free camera traversal around and inside the generated house, and Regenerate producing a new seed and visibly different valid generated house. Automated regression must prove house-catalog parity, prop applicability, deterministic same-seed replay, new-seed variation, socket/clearance correctness, selection/regeneration cleanup, and no stale geometry/resources after repeated changes. Follow `AGENTS.md`, `SceneIssues/README.md`, and `SceneIssues/feature-readme.md`; keep the feature open until all acceptance and built-player visual evidence are complete.
resolutionSummary: Added a production-backed HouseShowcase with canonical house/prop queries, palette-constrained socket furnishing, deterministic seed/regeneration behavior, reusable production shell articulation, built-player camera/UI inspection, cleanup, and module-local Structures validation. Final visual acceptance was corrected in shared production authoring/camera framing and revalidated through the standalone player.
